ruling.recommended_action: Refer the fare to a RydeHELP human reviewer: check whether the 22:54–23:03 deviation was actually driven on Guillemard Road (driver's path/road-name data) and decide the RD-5 scope; if the segment is confirmed unexempted, refund 2.13 km × $1.4102/km = $3.00 as a voucher and flag the driver's account (RD-6, 2 prior upheld route disputes, F18).
ruling.reasoning: The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride, 13.6 km driven against an 11.0 km optimal route (+2.6 km, +24%) [F1], and the record contains exactly one off-route segment: 22:54–23:03, 3.77 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, +2.13 km, up to 1095 m off route [F3]. Because RD-1 sets no threshold, that segment is the one that must be tested against RD-3, RD-4 and RD-5 [F3][RD-1]. The trace settles that no RD-4(a) incident exists, and speed-band data cannot exempt a segment on its own [F15][RD-4]; the band-2 PIE reading for 22:32–22:54 [F12] does not cover the 22:54–23:03 segment, so the driver's congestion explanation in his statement [F11] is corroboration only [F12][F15][RD-4]. The RD-6 precondition is on file: the driver has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days [F18][RD-6]. The decisive question is RD-5 scope. The driver asked "mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?" at 22:51 [F8] and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead." at 22:51 [F9], both timestamped in a complete chat record [F10], before the segment start of 22:54 [F3]; so there is rider consent, in the rider's own words, before the segment [F9][RD-5]. But a yes to a named road covers driving on that road only, and the record must tie the segment to that road: there is no stop on Guillemard Road, no message placing the car there, and no road-name fact for the driven path, while the driver's own post-trip statement [F11] is not consent and names no alternative road either [F3][F8][F9][F10][F11][RD-5]. Both advocates read F3 the same way — named_road_untied — so the scope of the agreed route is not settled by the record, and under RD-5/G13 the segment is undetermined rather than exempt or counted. That finding changes the amount, so it cannot be resolved by a ruling here. The fare arithmetic is otherwise clean: distance fare $19.15 over 13.58 km = $1.4102/km [F7], which on the 2.13 km segment would give 2.13 × 1.4102 = $3.0042 → $3.00 (the trace's formula); the billed excess distance of 2.59 km / $3.65 [F4] is not the segment figure. The $0.11 waiting item is a metered RydeTAXI waiting unit [F5][RD-3], no surge applied [F6] and the breakdown shows only published items [F7][FARE-1], so nothing else is refundable. With the money element undetermined, the case goes to a human.
ruling.escalation_reason: segment finding undetermined for F3; evidence unknown: The record does not settle whether the 22:54–23:03 off-route segment [F3] was driven on the agreed named road (Guillemard Road) [F8][F9]: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, the driver's statement [F11] is post-trip and names no other road, and no positioning message or stop ties the segment to the agreed road [RD-5, G13]. The amount depends on this finding.

segment_findings.reason: The rider's own pre-segment message "Sure, go ahead." [F9] at 22:51 answers the driver's ask about the named road Guillemard Road [F8], both timestamped earlier than the 22:54 segment start [F10][F3], so consent exists under RD-5; but consent to a named road covers only driving on that road, and nothing in the record ties this segment to Guillemard Road — no stop, no locating message, no road-name fact — while the driver's post-trip statement [F11] is not consent and names no other road [RD-5]. The scope is therefore untied and the segment is undetermined (G13), which changes the amount and sends the case to a person.

rejected_claims.reason: The $3.00 figure itself follows the RD-2 formula (2.13 km × $1.4102/km [F3][F7][RD-2]), but the claim that the segment is unexempted and refundable now cannot be executed: the rider's own pre-segment agreement to Guillemard Road [F8][F9] leaves the segment's scope untied by any record fact, so it is undetermined under RD-5/G13, not counted [F3][F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

The 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F18] can only support an additional action once this case is made out against the driver under RD-6; the segment remains undetermined [F3][RD-5][RD-6], so no flag_account attaches at this stage.

Correct that no RD-4(a) incident exists [F15][RD-4], but the absence of the incident exemption does not convert an untied-scope consent segment into a counted one; the rider's agreement to the named road [F8][F9] predates the segment [F3], so the segment is undetermined under RD-5/G13, not automatically RD-2-refundable [RD-5].

The arithmetic point is sound — the billed 2.59 km / $3.65 excess [F4] is not the segment figure, and the waiting unit $0.11 [F5] stays with the driver under RD-3 — but the conclusion that nothing is owed cannot be reached while the segment's coverage is undetermined [F3][F8][F9][RD-2][RD-3].
